notes:
Summary: Enterprise evaluation for Dedicated capacity. Primary ask: guaranteed throughput & latency SLOs for customer-facing chat + embedding heavy background jobs. They want reserved GPU planning, clear autoscaling semantics, and SLA credit language.

POC & technical constraints: want 95th/99th p99 latency SLOs documented (CTO: "we cannot accept >200ms p99 for front-door chat"). Target steady-state throughput: 500–800 qps for short-text chat paths; burst to 1.8k qps for marketing peaks. Background embedding pipeline: 10–15k embeddings/hr with batched jobs.

Autoscaling / capacity management specifics discussed:
- Scale-up: prefer predictive + reactive hybrid. Use metric-based (queue-depth + CPU/GPU utilization) with pre-warm triggers from traffic forecasts (cron + traffic anomaly detector).
- Warm pools: proposal: maintain small warm pool of 8–12 pre-warmed GPU workers for chat model to eliminate cold-starts on 2x bursts. Warm pool warmup target: under 45s.
- Scale-down: conservative cooldown to avoid oscillation; suggested min-up window 10min, graceful drain with max queue depth backpressure.
- Queueing behavior: bounded request queue per model route, backpressure response with HTTP 429 + retry-after; route-level SLA tiers (gold/silver) to prioritize latency-sensitive traffic.
- Reserved GPU planning: blend static reserved capacity for baseline + autoscale for bursts. Customer prefers commit for 40% of peak to reduce unit cost.
- Throughput guarantees: Redwood to commit to 95% of agreed throughput during business hours, with documented fallback model variants and cross-region failover.
- SLA negotiation points: SLA credits for p99/P95 misses, definition of measurement windows, scheduled maintenance blackouts, and data residency enforcement. Legal flagged indemnity language and disaster recovery RTO targets.

Commercial: preliminary estimate shows $250k–$1M ARR depending on reserved GPU mix and burst margins. They are cost sensitive but prioritize latency & reliability for trading-supporting chat.
